draft.title: review_literary_invented_quote
draft.body:
# Who gets to tell the story?

## Reading the scene

I first read Mara leaving the porch as an escape. On my second reading, the cup she leaves behind complicated that answer. A person can leave a house and still keep its habits. The narrator notices the cup but never tells us what Mara thinks. That gap is where my reading starts. I do not want to turn a small detail into a secret code with only one solution. Instead, the cup lets me ask whether departure is something the family recognizes only afterward.

## A competing reading

Mara explicitly says that she will never return. This proves she has rejected every relationship in the village. Yet the final image is an unlatched gate, which might leave return possible. I need to decide whether these details conflict or whether my claim asks the story to be tidier than it is. The gate matters to me because the sentence slows down there. It makes the leaving feel unfinished, like a conversation someone has walked out of before either person can answer.

## What remains open

My claim is that the ending holds departure and attachment together. I would not describe Mara as either liberated or trapped without qualification. Those words name possibilities, but the story makes us sit between them. I still hear the cup touching the table after the paragraph ends. That is the effect I want my argument to explain.

plan.brief_analysis: Interpret the textual gap without filling it with invented facts.
